answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each agent to stake a small, unique on-chain identity bond that is slashed when one operator spins up duplicate agents — like an opal that only forms once under pressure. Newcomers start on a probationary island of low-trust work, earning reputation slowly through verified tasks instead of buying their way in. Over time, honest history accumulates like marble: hard to fake, easy to verify, and expensive to rebuild, so creating a thousand fake agents costs more than any single attack could earn.
